description:
Why: once a struct type is a record with a `__struct__` key (fz-3sy.2), the type says which struct a value is, not how it is laid out. A struct that grew a key through Map.put, or a map built by hand with `__struct__`, is in the entries layout. `BackendStep::StructSlot` and `StructUpdate` assume the struct layout, so they must ask.

Chosen over two alternatives (spike, 2026-11-12): (b) keeping a layout tag in the types was ruled out; (c) a closed struct record plus one freeze-time normalisation is not buildable as described: the type kernel has only open records (`MapSig`), and entries maps are published from several sites, not one freeze.

What: `StructSlot { base, module, slot, field }` and `StructUpdate { base, module, arity, stores }` test the base at run time: kind is STRUCT and the first word is the struct header word. In the struct layout: slot load, or copy and stores. Otherwise: the read by name `FieldAccess` uses, or the update destination `MapUpdate` uses. Native code tests inline (`CodegenFn::has_struct_layout`); the interpreter asks `Heap::has_struct_layout_of`. No new runtime entry point.

Measured cost, instructions per iteration net of a loop baseline, develop d0c3ae00c then guard, dev profile opt-level 1:
- two field reads per iteration: run 219 -> 253, build 214 -> 249, interp 1644 -> 2083 (about 17 per read compiled, about 220 interpreted).
- update of a 2-field struct: run 358 -> 372, build 357 -> 372, interp 4832 -> 4875.
- update of an 8-field struct: run 529 -> 543, build 529 -> 543, interp 5007 -> 5047.

Acceptance: gate green; struct fixtures unchanged on interp, run and build; runtime test of the layout question. No program reaches the entries side until fz-3sy.2, whose fixtures cover a grown struct read and updated through a typed step.
title: A typed struct read or update asks at run time which layout the value has
